$description: Contextual Workspace capability navigation. The capability capsule IS the capability list: one horizontal row of entries, bounded in width, whose overflow strategy is internal scrolling rather than a menu. #1347 Capsule V2 supersedes the two rules this pattern previously carried — that direct chrome is bounded to the contextually-justified set, and that everything else is disclosed through More/menu. The bound the design keeps is on the capsule, not on the entry count: the capsule must remain inside the tool bar while its content scrolls. Two conditions decide a slot, and both are Nession's: the capability must have a Workspace view, and it must not be `unavailable`. `unavailable` resolves to `hidden` presence, which is dropped before the row is built, so the row never carries a dead entry — an exclusion #1347 did not touch. Every other state keeps its slot, publishing `data-capability-state` / `data-capability-presence` rather than changing the row's membership. The active capability carries a selected state and is scrolled into view. The capsule is the capability root's control: it is present at the capability root and absent once the user pushes into capability-owned detail. The App band is a compact pill floating over the work surface, so it declares its own touch floor instead of the 44px chrome default: chrome yields before the work surface, and the entries are secondary controls the user reaches deliberately rather than in a hurry (#730). The entries' targets are sized by `experience.{web,app}.dockTarget` (32px on Web, 28px on App) rather than `control-md`: on App control-md is 44px by design (`experience/app.json` forbids any app control below the 44px floor), so borrowing it would grow this band back past the compact floor recorded above. The two agree on App by construction — both are 28px — and this contract's assertion is the floor that keeps them from diverging.
